text.p: The Turkish lira closed easier at 89,260 to the dollar on Friday after Thursday's 89,030 on a higher central bank dollar rate for banks' currency transfers.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory monthly foreign currency transfers at 89,125 lira, up from 88,900 at yesterday's close.
The lira dived to a low of 89,400 to the dollar earlier in the day in line with the dollar's gains in world markets, but firmed to 89,260 at the close on the dollar's fall against the mark.

The money market opened with a 32 trillion lira surplus and overnight money traded between 65-74.50 percent in the day. But the central bank stepped in to lend 10.2 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent at the close to cover banks facing shortages ahead of the weekend.
The average overnight rate was slightly lower at 70.27 percent after 70.97 on Thursday when the central bank had drained 1.4 trillion lira at 50 percent.
In the t-bill market, yields dropped by around one percentage point across the board on higher liquidity earlier in the day.
The yield on the most actively traded March 12, 1997 paper, sold at an average of 128.92 percent in Tuesday's Treasury auction, fell to 124.24 percent from Thursday's 124.51 percent average.
The second most heavily traded February 26 paper yielded 123.44 percent after 123.73 yesterday.
